To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The production rate of light antinuclei is consistent with expectations from the coalescence model, 2) The production rate is not consistent with expectations from thermal models.

(i) the production of antiprotons is enhanced by a factor of 2.4 with respect to the expectation from a coalescence of pions and kaons, and (ii) the enhancement of the production of antihyperons is even larger, by a factor of about 5, and (iii) this enhancement is observed for central collisions only.
we have measured a large amount of antiprotons in heavy-ion collisions, and that the antiprotons are not produced in pairs, but are mostly produced singly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of antinuclei production, especially antihelium production.
the production of antinuclei in heavy ion collisions.
the production of light antinuclei in the CERN SPS energy range and with the search for strangelets in the same range.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the production of light (anti)nucleus is in good agreement with the expectations from coalescence models.
the production of antinuclei is consistent with the production of nucleons.
the production of antinuclei is not suppressed compared to the production of antiprotons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the production of light nuclei and antinuclei at CERN SIS energies is consistent with a thermal model and that a coalescence description of antinuclei is possible for the most central collisions only.
antinuclei production at SPS is well explained by coalescence.
the production of light (anti)nucleus in heavy ion collisions is well explained by coalescence of nucleons and antinucleons from the source.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the production of light antinuclei is suppressed with respect to the expectation from the statistical model.
the measured antideuteron yield is in agreement with the prediction of the coalescence model and the antiproton yield is in agreement both with the coalescence and the thermodynamical model.
the measured antinuclei production rates are compatible with expectations from a statistical model.
